title: Microeconomic Guardrails: cost-aware microbatch heuristics and compact quant presets
author: Maya Krishnan
description: Context: teams routinely hit regressions where aggressive microbatching or permissive quant presets reduce cost but cause tail latency or quality issues in mixed workloads. This PR introduces a lightweight runtime guardrail layer that estimates per-request marginal token cost and enforces conservative defaults for microbatching and compact quant profiles by default. Motivation: provide an opt-out, observable set of defaults that protect SLAs while still enabling meaningful unit-econ wins for typical web-scale inference traffic. Changes in this PR: 1) runtime/scheduler: add MicrobatchPolicy that chooses per-route microbatch ceilings based on recent token-cost distribution and a simple short-window SLO classifier; 2) optimize/cost_estimator: introduce estimator that computes a marginal-cost-per-token delta for quant profiles and batching modes (approximate, fast, cache-friendly); 3) config/defaults: add cost_guardrails.v1 containing default target_tradeoff (safety-first), max_microbatch_tokens, compact_quant_safety_margin and rollout flags; 4) CLI/console: surface a new page and CLI flags to preview expected cost/latency impact before enabling a profile; 5) e2e tests + smoke: add workload fixtures that simulate mixed short/long sequence workloads and validate no >2x tail latency regression; 6) docs: add a guide and recommended on-ramp for converting existing autoscale/batching configs to the new guarded presets. Implementation notes: MicrobatchPolicy uses a rolling 2-minute window (configurable) of (tokens, latency, success) samples to estimate a safety-bound microbatch_token_limit = max(16, median_tokens * safety_multiplier) subject to an absolute ceiling. The cost_estimator is intentionally conservative: it weights observed runtime token cost with quantized-mode delta calibrated from offline kernel benchmarks and per-instance throughput counters. Defaults: target_tradeoff="safety", safety_multiplier=1.1, max_microbatch_tokens=1024, compact_quant_safety_margin=0.07. Backwards compatibility: the guardrails are opt-out by route via config.allow_guardrails=false. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on staging for 48h, then 10% production canary for 72h, then gradual 100% if no regressions. Metrics & alerts: new metrics redwood.costguard.microbatch_ceiling, redwood.costguard.violations, redwood.costest.estimated_delta; alert if costguard.violations > 0.5% of traffic for 1h or if p99 latency regresses > 15% vs baseline. Testing: unit tests for policy math, mocked estimator harness, end-to-end smoke tests with perf lab harness; manual benching on small GPU pool included in PR. Docs & examples: updated quickstarts to include recommended presets for chat vs completion routes. Security & compliance: no secrets changes. Known limitations: the estimator does not currently account for multi-tenant interference; follow-up ENG ticket upserts detection and tenancy-aware calibration. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit + e2e tests - [x] docs - [x] canary/rollback plan - [x] metrics and alerts - [x] performance smoke in perf-lab

release_notes: Introduce opt-out runtime guardrails for microbatching and compact quant profiles that provide conservative defaults to protect latency SLAs while enabling cost reductions. New metrics and console previews added. Rollout under feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag cost_guardrails_enabled=false by default in existing clusters. During canary set to true for 10% of traffic using rollout controller. Watch redwood.costguard.violations and redwood.costest.estimated_delta. Rollback by toggling flag or reverting to previous scheduler (main).
